title: The Word of Christ, Our Lord
description: The Word of Christ, Our Lord in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 133, “The word quick and powerful. Heb 4:12,13”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The word of Christ, our Lord, With whom we have to do; Is sharp-er than a two edged sword, To pierce the sin-ner through.

lines: The word of Christ, our Lord,
With whom we have to do;
Is sharper than a two-edged sword,
It fills the conscience with amaze,
Each thought and purpose stands revealed,
He counts their sighs and falling tears,
And helps them from on high.
Yea, all they would do, if they could,
For all the evil deeds they do,
And all they would have done.
Are marked and known by thee;
Afford us, Lord, thy light of grace

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
